description: The bar chart illustrates the number of samples associated with different reasoning categories. The categories are shown on the horizontal axis as rotated labels in the following left-to-right order: Mathematical Reasoning, General Reasoning, Natural Scene Reasoning, Physical Reasoning, Logical Puzzle Reasoning, and Chemical Reasoning; no explicit x-axis title is shown. The vertical axis is labeled “Number of Samples” and uses a logarithmic scale with major tick marks labeled at approximately \(10^2\), \(10^3\), and \(10^4\). Each category is represented by a single light-blue vertical bar, with some bars annotated by numeric values above them: General Reasoning is labeled 1709, Natural Scene Reasoning is labeled 413, Physical Reasoning is labeled 232, Logical Puzzle Reasoning is labeled 91, and Chemical Reasoning is labeled 49. The Mathematical Reasoning bar is the tallest and reaches close to the \(10^4\) tick (with a small gray segment at the very top of the bar), while the shortest bar is Chemical Reasoning at 49; the bars appear arranged from higher to lower counts from left to right, and there is no legend or additional visual emphasis beyond the value annotations and the small gray cap on the Mathematical Reasoning bar.
